EPIDEMIC CONTEXT — Q1 2024 (SE01–SE13) coincides with a major dengue epidemic in Brazil; case volumes are exceptionally high and may stress reporting systems, causing delays, retroactive revisions, and non-standard bulletin formats.
DATA LAG — SINAN data is subject to notification lag; preliminary figures published during Q1 2024 may differ substantially from consolidated figures published post-quarter.

SUBNATIONAL GRANULARITY — Brazilian states (UFs) and municipalities publish independent bulletins; national SVS figures may not match the sum of state-level figures due to reporting timing differences.

LANGUAGE — Primary official sources are in Brazilian Portuguese; query terms and extraction logic must accommodate Portuguese-language field labels (e.g., 'casos prováveis', 'óbitos', 'internações', 'semana epidemiológica').
SEROTYPE CONTEXT — DENV-3 re-emergence was reported in Brazil in late 2023–2024; serotype data may be relevant for outbreak characterization but is not required for core case count extraction.
HOSPITALIZATION DATA — Hospitalization counts (internações) may require cross-referencing SIH-SUS data, which is published separately from SINAN case notification data and may have longer lag times.
GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE — Brazil has 26 states + 1 Federal District (DF); subnational_location should capture UF (estado) and locality should capture município where available.
CUMULATIVE vs. INCIDENT COUNTS — Distinguish between cumulative totals (acumulado) and weekly incident counts (casos na semana) in all extracted records; annotate accordingly in evidence_quote.

iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Coverage is substantially sufficient for the Q1 2024 Brazil dengue task across most target fields. Confirmed source candidates span: (1) Brazilian federal MoH/SVSA official bulletins (gov.br — SE 4 bulletin, March 2024 weekly semanal via static.poder360.com.br); (2) COE-Dengue weekly informes covering SE 01–11 (Scribd/COE Informe SE 06) and SE 01–05 (sindag.org.br COE Informe 01); (3) PAHO Q1-specific press release dated March 28, 2024 (paho.org) confirming Brazil accounts for 83% of Americas cases and 87% of deaths; (4) Health Policy Watch article citing PAHO's "over one million cases in first six weeks of 2024" figure; (5) State-level sources: Minas Gerais (saude.mg.gov.br), Distrito Federal (saude.df.gov.br), Paraná (dengue.pr.gov.br), Rio de Janeiro (sistemas.saude.rj.gov.br), Goiás (goias.gov.br), Rio Grande do Sul (cevs.rs.gov.br); (6) InfoDengue (info.dengue.mat.br) and open data (dadosabertos.saude.gov.br) for structured database coverage; (7) Academic/PMC sources (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov) for corroboration. Key remaining gap: São Paulo state-specific Q1 2024 bulletin was not confirmed in results, and a direct COE-Dengue source on the gov.br domain for SE 1–13 was not surfaced (only a Scribd mirror and a sindag.org.br mirror). However, the PAHO March 28 press release and the COE informes provide sufficient Q1-specific national-level quantitative anchors.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: High. The most authoritative sources are confirmed present: (a) gov.br domain (Brazilian federal MoH/SVSA) — highest trust for national case/death counts; (b) paho.org — independent international validation dated March 28, 2024, squarely within Q1 2024; (c) COE-Dengue informes (SE 01–05 and SE 01–11) — official emergency committee reports, even if accessed via mirrors (sindag.org.br, Scribd), the document provenance is COE/SVSA; (d) State health secretariat domains (saude.mg.gov.br, saude.df.gov.br, dengue.pr.gov.br, sistemas.saude.rj.gov.br) — authoritative for subnational data. Lower-trust sources (agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br, healthpolicy-watch.news, nytimes.com) are present as corroborating news sources that explicitly cite MoH/PAHO figures. No unverified aggregators or blogs without named official sources are being relied upon as primary evidence.
